identity.title: Multiwavelength ALMA Imaging of HD 34282: Dust-trapping Signatures of a Vortex Candidate

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present sub-$0.1''$ resolution ALMA continuum observations of the HD 34282 disk at 0.9, 1.3, 2.1, and 3.1 mm.

evidence.quote: HD 34282 is a Herbig Ae star located at a distance of 309$\pm$2 pc
HD 34282 is a Herbig Ae star located at a distance of 309$\pm$2 pc

question.value: Is the bright azimuthal mm arc in the HD 34282 disk consistent with dust trapping in a vortex, as tested by its multi-wavelength morphology, spectral index and peak shifts?

evidence.quote: enable us to probe the physical origin of the arc.

method.value: ALMA pipeline, flag lines, average to 6 s and 8 channels, self-calibrate SB then concatenated, align with exoALMA tools

evidence.quote: the data was averaged in time to 6 seconds and in frequency over 8 channels.
The peak SNR was improved by 42$\%$ after the self-calibration.

analysis_steps.goal: Parametric visibility fit for geometry and arc radius

method.value: galario fit of three Gaussian rings and 2D Gaussian arc, Gaussian likelihood, emcee

evidence.quote: The visibilities are modeled with three Gaussian rings and a 2D Gaussian arc.

fitting.value: Two-step coarse-to-fine emcee; Band 7 first then initialises others; amplitudes uniform in log

evidence.quote: We start with the high-S/N Band 7 data, then use its posterior medians to initialize independent fits for Bands 3, 4, and 6

validation.value: Residual images: noise-like at 3.1 and 2.1 mm, >10σ at 1.3 and 0.9 mm

evidence.quote: At 1.3 and 0.9 mm, residual structures at $>10\sigma$ level remain

analysis_steps.goal: Remove axisymmetric emission and measure arc peak and width

method.value: Deproject, frank 1D radial reconstruction, subtract, image residuals, subtract background profile from 180° opposite, measure peak and FWHM

evidence.quote: We subtract the `frank` model from the visibilities, image the residuals, and measure the arc peak location and full width at half maximum (FWHM)
The hyper-parameters are set to $\alpha = 1.3$ and $w_\mathrm{smooth} = 0.01$

validation.value: Bootstrap, 500 realizations adding Gaussian noise at map RMS

evidence.quote: We estimate the statistical uncertainties of the arc peak location and azimuthal width using a bootstrap approach for 500 realizations.

method.value: tau = -ln[1 - I/B(Tdust)] with Tdust 29.6 K; galario-model based estimate; scattering via Zhu 2019 relation

evidence.quote: We estimate $\tau_\nu$ at each wavelength using a toy model based on the Eddington-Barbier approximation in an isothermal slab

assumptions.value: Dust and gas thermally coupled; constant temperature in azimuth; albedo up to 0.8 (0.7 representative)

evidence.quote: we adopt a constant dust temperature with azimuth.

validation.value: Compared image-based vs galario-model-based estimates; ±5 K changes tau by 25-30%

evidence.quote: a $\pm 5$ K change in $T_{\rm dust}$ would alter $\tau_\nu$ by $\sim$25-30% in the arc

method.value: Align images, convolve to common beam, alpha = ln(I1/I2)/ln(nu1/nu2) where SNR>15

evidence.quote: We compute the spectral index only for regions with SNR $>15$ in both bands.

validation.value: Compared with baseline-corrected arc and galario model images

evidence.quote: we also compute $\alpha$ from the best-fit `galario` model images

analysis_steps.goal: Stokes number and comparison with vortex predictions

method.value: St = pi rho_s a /(2 Sigma_gas) with a = lambda/2pi, rho_s=1 g/cm3, Sigma_gas=2.6 g/cm2; compare width and peak shift trends

evidence.quote: We assume that emission at each wavelength is dominated by a characteristic size $a \sim\lambda_{\mathrm{obs}}/2\pi$ (cite: Draine_2006) and take $\rho_s = 1~\mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$.

findings_qualitative.value: Arc sits in a double-gap, triple-ring disk; 0.9 mm shows arc shoulder, dimmer near-side ring and faint inner arc at r~0.17"

evidence.quote: We also detect a faint, azimuthally extended arc at $r \sim 0.17''$ with $\sim7\sigma$ significance

claims.hypothesis: Arc narrows azimuthally at longer wavelengths as expected for dust trapping
claims.experiment: frank-residual arc FWHM at four wavelengths
claims.result: FWHM falls from 65.8° to 37.1° from 0.9 to 3.1 mm

evidence.quote: The azimuthal width of the arc decreases monotonically toward longer wavelengths

claims.hypothesis: Peak shifts follow vortex predictions for low Stokes numbers
claims.experiment: Arc peak azimuth vs wavelength with St estimate
claims.result: No shift among 1.3-3.1 mm; 15±4° shift at 0.9 mm opposite to rotation
claims.finding: Longer wavelengths consistent; 0.9 mm shift likely optical depth or temperature

evidence.quote: Our 1.3, 2.1 and 3.1 mm measurements are consistent with this expectation

claims.hypothesis: Arc has larger grains or higher dust density than the ring
claims.result: alpha 2.48 in arc vs 3.11 in ring
claims.finding: Consistent with enhanced grain growth and/or surface density

evidence.quote: The spectral index reaches its minimum at the arc

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Eccentric-disk apocenter pile-up cannot be excluded; unresolved optically thick clumps cannot be excluded

evidence.quote: we cannot formally exclude the possibility that the arc consists of unresolved optically thick clumps

limitations_admitted.value: Arc may be optically thick at 0.9 mm; vortex origin not unique; need longer-wavelength and gas kinematics

evidence.quote: A definitive test will require longer-wavelength continuum data to constrain the grain-size distribution

referee_caveats_inferred: Stokes number rests on a single assumed grain size and gas surface density from another paper
galario model fails at 1.3 and 0.9 mm, and model-based optical depths are only at 3.1 and 2.1 mm
